match.reason: No point in the bank covers ethical behaviour in marketing; corporate social responsibility is a broader idea about doing good beyond legal duties, not truthful and fair marketing practices.

rejected.title: Ethics in marketing
card: Ethics are standards of right and wrong. An ethical marketer does more than obey the law. They ask whether a practice is fair and honest to customers and rivals.
Truthful
Ads should give an honest picture of a product, its price and what it can do. Hiding or twisting facts to win a sale is unethical.
Children
Children are easily influenced, so marketers should avoid promoting harmful products to them, such as tobacco or vaping products.
Fair competition
Marketers should win sales by offering a better product, not by spreading lies about rivals. Selling must not be disguised as research, such as a fake survey that is really a sales pitch.
rejected.remember: Ethical marketing is honest, protects children, competes fairly and keeps selling separate from research.

a.q: Which action is an example of unethical marketing?
opts: Phoning people for a survey, then pushing a sales offer
Running ads that show the product's real price
Offering a better product than a rival does
Ending a campaign that is not working
a.why: Using a survey as a cover for a sales pitch disguises selling as research, which is unethical. Showing the real price is honest, and offering a better product is fair competition.
a.clue: Which action hides its real purpose from the customer?

b.q: Sunny Fizz, a drink company in Perth, sets up a stall at a primary school. It gives out free cans of a very sugary drink and says they are healthy. Which is the best ethical criticism?
opts: It promotes a harmful product to children with a false claim
It lets a rival win customers by offering a lower price
It spends money on a stall instead of a national campaign
It gives away free cans that people would usually pay for
b.why: The firm targets children with a harmful product and makes an untrue claim about it. Free samples are not unethical on their own, so the giveaway is not the main problem. Competing on price is fair.
b.clue: Look at who is being targeted and what is being said about the product.

draft.title: Ethics in marketing
card: Ethics are standards of right and wrong. An ethical marketer asks whether a practice is fair and honest, not only whether it is legal.
Truthful
Marketers should give an honest picture of a product, its price and what it can do. Twisting or hiding facts to win a sale is unethical.
Children
Children are easily influenced and cannot judge a sales message well. Marketers should avoid promoting harmful products to them.
Fair play
Marketers should win sales with a better offer, not by attacking rivals unfairly. Selling must never be disguised as research, such as a sales pitch posing as a survey.
draft.remember: An ethical marketer is honest, protects children, competes fairly and keeps selling and research apart.

a.q: A caller says she is running a survey on home security. After three questions she starts selling an alarm system. What is the ethical problem?
opts: Selling has been disguised as research
The alarm system is too expensive
The survey had too few questions
A rival could copy the sales offer
a.why: The caller used the look of research to cover a sales pitch, which is unethical. Price and survey length are not the ethical issue here. A rival copying the offer has nothing to do with honesty.
a.clue: Ask what the caller said she was doing and what she was really doing.

b.q: Sunny Fizz, a drink company in Perth, hands out free cans of a very sugary drink at a primary school. Staff tell the children it is a health drink. What is the best ethical criticism?
opts: It targets children with a harmful product and a false claim
It pays for a stall instead of running a wider campaign
It gives out free cans that people usually pay for
It gives rivals a chance to win customers with lower prices
b.why: The firm aims a harmful product at children and makes an untrue claim about it. Free samples are not unethical on their own, so the giveaway is not the main problem. Rivals winning customers on price is fair competition.
b.clue: Look at who is being targeted and what is being said about the product.

a.best: Selling has been disguised as research

b.best: It targets children with a harmful product and a false claim
